codeReview.summary: Successfully consolidated 50 pre-existing individual #[test] functions into 4 well-structured table-driven test functions. The refactoring is clean, uses good diagnostic messages, and preserves all previously-tested behavior. One minor improvement opportunity: 10 ToggleItem variants (Pump2–Pump6, Blower, Light2, HoldMode, HeatingMode, TemperatureRange) have .code() coverage in toggle_item_code_table but lack explicit Command::ToggleItem().encode() coverage in command_encode_table. This is a pre-existing coverage gap (not a regression) — the encode path is trivially `vec![0x11, item.code(), 0x00]`, so code() coverage implicitly validates encode. The refactoring is correctly classified as non-blocking since the original tests had the same gap.

issues.description: command_encode_table tests only 12 of 21 ToggleItem variants via Command::ToggleItem().encode(). Missing: Pump2, Pump3, Pump4, Pump5, Pump6, Blower, Light2, HoldMode, HeatingMode, TemperatureRange. This is a pre-existing coverage gap (the original 50 tests also omitted these), but the table-driven format makes it easy to add them. The encode logic is trivially `vec![0x11, item.code(), 0x00]`, so the toggle_item_code_table test provides implicit coverage of the key mapping.
